recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the current-build FHIR-31792 application without broadening into separate legacy ModelInfo resource-name cleanup or deciding the related bidirectional-link issues.
issue_request: FHIR-31792 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested changing the packaging/authorization relationship so the marketing authorization points to the packaged product rather than PackagedProductDefinition carrying a back-reference, with RegulatedAuthorization.subject able to reference multiple authorized products.
initial_application: Prior FHIR-31792 commits 05841da3edffbd41949d8547c323362859a1e998 and a404d9f6bc55cfff0a33603371eb935e919031c7 removed PackagedProductDefinition.marketingAuthorization and the RegulatedAuthorization target from the PackagedProductDefinition StructureDefinition. Commits dc008bd65482b3817a2a818883be30aa83d77986 and f16b0ee38e70c7e874b1330dc0c8624becc7f8d8 changed RegulatedAuthorization.subject to 0..*. The current authoritative resource definitions were therefore already correct, but the active FHIR ModelInfo Library still exposed the old MedicinalProductPackaged.marketingAuthorization element.
additional_context: FHIR-31792 cites FHIR-31782, FHIR-31859, and FHIR-31862 as the same BRR bidirectional-link cleanup family, but this reconciliation only needed to decide FHIR-31792. source/fhir.ini keeps PackagedProductDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, and Library active/approved, and source/library/list-Library-examples.xml lists Library/library-fhir-model-definition as a current FHIR ModelInfo Library example. BRR minutes confirm agreement to change the reference direction and no Zulip evidence contradicted the Jira/source conclusion.
